surprises.body: Anaheim’s bottom-six forwards played 35% of the forwards’ 5-on-5 time, against their usual 43% and a league average of 42%. A team strays this far about once every 250 games. That’s rarer than once a season for any one team.

story.head: Luneau sparks a Ducks comeback
paras: It was a busy first period. William Strömgren struck first for the Flames early in the period, but Jeff Malott tied it 1-1 for Anaheim 27 seconds later. Joel Hanley and Joel Farabee scored two and a half minutes apart late in the period to put the Flames up 3-1, and that was all they would get. Anaheim pulled Lukáš Dostál after three goals and turned to Ville Husso to start the second. Tristan Luneau cut Calgary’s lead to 3-2 midway through the second, and Leo Carlsson made it 3-3 on the power play just 55 seconds into the third. Cutter Gauthier put the Ducks ahead for good with a minute and a half left, his fifth straight game with a goal. Nikita Nesterenko sealed it into the empty net with 14 seconds left.

The Ducks had the better of the chances, outshooting the Flames 29-21. Dustin Wolf stopped 24 of 28 for the Flames. The Ducks improved to 9-7-1, fourth in the Pacific, while the Flames dropped to 7-9-1, fifth in the Pacific.

items.text: Four straight wins for the Ducks.
Cutter Gauthier has a point in seven straight games, with a goal in each of the last five.
Leo Carlsson extended his point streak against Calgary to seven games.
With Maxim Tsyplakov out, Strömgren took his spot and scored.
